source.title: RouteREPA: Routed Representation Alignment for Just Image Transformers
source.authors: Yi Tan; Beier Zhu; Sirui Chen; Cheng Chen; Xingyu Zhu; Yuan Zhou; Zhenshan Tan; Tianrun Chen; Hanwang Zhang

record.tranche_reason: The study uses representation alignment (REPA) as a training method and baseline, but does not test whether independently trained models converge in representation geometry as scale or capability increases.
record.gate_note: The paper measures JiT representations' alignment to DINOv2 and studies how routing and noise timestep affect that alignment. These results concern a generator-to-teacher alignment objective, not convergence between independently trained models, cross-modal model alignment, or robustness of convergence across similarity measures. The paper also reports reconstruction results, which do not directly measure the claim's versions.
record.test_reason: The paper uses REPA, an objective aligning diffusion features to DINOv2, as a training tool and reports mainly its routed variant's generation performance. Its one analysis of naturally arising alignment (Fig. 2a) compares a single pixel-space and latent-space JiT pair with no scale or capability sweep. That is not a test of convergence with scale, across seeds or modalities, or across metrics. The other CKNNA results (Fig. 4a) measure alignment that is deliberately induced by the REPA/RouteREPA loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors find a conflict between DINOv2 alignment and pixel reconstruction in JiT and propose routing to resolve it. They make no claims about representational convergence.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains pixel-space and latent-space diffusion transformers with REPA or the proposed routed variant, and measures CKNNA against DINOv2. It does not apply a method for testing cross-model convergence.
record.method_sensitivity: CKNNA alignment differs by representation type and routed branch, and the reported alignment-route comparison with REPA varies with flow timestep. Routing behavior also varies across network depth and training stage.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched generation quality (FID about 31), with the same architecture and training recipe, pixel-space JiT shows substantially lower CKNNA to DINOv2 than a VAE-latent JiT (Fig. 2a).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For generative models of matched capability, alignment to a discriminative encoder depends on the input space (pixels versus pretrained latents), not on capability alone.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the RouteREPA loss, alignment-routed features exceed REPA's CKNNA as noise decreases, while generation-routed features stay less aligned (Fig. 4a).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under an explicit alignment objective, alignment to a teacher can be confined to a routed subset of channels.

record.problems: The relevant CKNNA results are shown in figures without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. Alignment is measured against a pretrained teacher rather than between independently trained models; the paper does not test scale-dependent convergence or alternative similarity measures.
record.rows_left_out: Reconstruction MSE and LPIPS results in Figs. 2(b,c) and 4(b,c) are omitted because they measure decodability, not representation convergence. Other generation-quality and routing results do not measure the claim's versions.

untested.parts: No sweep of model size or capability for alignment to DINOv2. CKNNA is not reported across JiT-B/L/H.
No cross-model mapping or stitching. The decoder probes reconstruct pixels, not another model's features.
No feature or circuit universality analysis.
Only CKNNA is used. No variation of the metric, its neighbour count, or out-of-distribution inputs. The timestep dependence shown is within an alignment-trained model.
There is no test of a plateau and no attribution of alignment to shared data versus a common world model. Fig. 2a hints that input space affects alignment, but it rests on a single, figure-only pair.

record.verdict_notes: R1/R2 is the only naturally arising cross-model alignment result. It loosely bears on V7, since input space rather than capability drives alignment differences at matched FID. However, it is one figure-only pair with no numbers or uncertainty, so no verdict is given. CKNNA is used following REPA, which itself cites the Platonic Representation Hypothesis.

versions.untested_parts: The study varies representation branch and flow timestep, but does not test convergence across similarity measures, their settings, or input distributions.

relation.reason: The paper uses representation alignment as a training tool without testing any listed convergence version.

tranche.reason: Alignment is used as a training objective, with results evaluating routing and generation performance. The unforced JiT/Latent JiT comparison does not establish a trend or effect specified by a claim version.

source_check.notes: The alignment values are figure-only; the recorded qualitative comparisons are stated in the text. R3–R4 document the proposed method's induced alignment and should not be counted as independent convergence evidence.
